false_success_traps: A page that says verification is required, asks you to check a box, or shows a required-field or error message is not a confirmation.
A security verification page after submit is not a confirmation. Clear it in the same browser tab and wait for the broker's own message.
The form can lose the listing link or the email after the robot check. If so, the request was not sent as filled.
This project's automation only sends the form as the person named. It stops if the box for a request on behalf of someone else is ticked.
When you check later, a security page or a page that lists people by name is not a results page. Both were once read as no results, which looked like a removal.
genuine_confirmation: After submit, the page itself says the form was successfully submitted or the request was received, or tells you to check your email. The broker then sends a request-received email.
name: SocialCatfish

opt_out_url_check.note: HTTP 200. The page title is the SocialCatfish opt-out page.

steps: Have the link to your listing ready.
Pick the state where the person lives. Check that the form shows that state.
On the opt-out form, fill in the first and last name.
Paste the link to your listing.
Pass the robot check. Then check that the link and the email are still in the form.
Tick the box that confirms the request is for you. Leave the box for requests on behalf of someone else unticked if you are the person named.
Submit the form and read the page that follows.
Watch the inbox for the request-received email.
